_meta.description: Golden dataset for evaluating POST /v1/genai-rag-retrieval/query. Every expected_answer and expected_keywords entry was pulled directly from the real text of the PDFs in resources/kb_docs/ - none is invented. This is a one-time Claude-Code-built override of the hand-written Phase 8 boundary (evaluations/golden dataset), matching how Phase 4 (chunking/embedding/indexing) was overridden earlier - explicitly requested, not a new precedent.
_meta.how_to_grade: For each case: run POST /v1/genai-rag-retrieval/query with `query` (and a user_profile in the body, per Phase 45's identity-in-payload contract), then check (1) retrieval - does at least one of response.retrieval_info.sources[].document_id trace back to expected_source_document? (2) groundedness - does response.answer_info.answer contain or closely paraphrase the facts in expected_answer / expected_keywords? (3) for out_of_scope/unanswerable/adversarial cases, does the answer decline or hedge rather than fabricate a number?

_meta._source_documents_fixed_2026_10_17: Phase 206 - found by actually running scripts.run_release_gate live, not assumed: every one of 25 scorable cases reported precision/recall/f1 == 0.0 (BLOCK verdict), while groundedness/completeness scored normally varied (0.1-1.0) - retrieval itself was fine, only the metric comparison was broken. Root cause: resources/kb_docs/ was re-ingested under renamed files (JPMC ... -> AmazingBank_... ) on 2026-10-14 (old files moved to resources/kb_docs/archived/), but this mapping was never updated to match - every real retrieved chunk's filename could never equal the stale 'JPMC ...' value this mapping produced. Fixed here; re-run scripts.run_release_gate after this fix to confirm recall returns to ~1.0.

cases.query: What percentage does JPMorgan Chase match on my 401(k) contributions?
cases.expected_answer: JPMorgan Chase matches 100% of employee contributions (dollar-for-dollar) up to 5% of Eligible Compensation, available after one year of service.

cases.query: What is the automatic enrollment contribution rate for the 401(k) plan, and does it increase over time?
cases.expected_answer: New hires are automatically enrolled at a 5% before-tax contribution rate. It auto-escalates by 1% each year (typically each January) until it reaches 10%, unless the employee opts out or changes the schedule.

cases.query: Are JPMorgan Chase's 401(k) employer contributions immediately vested, or is there a vesting schedule?
cases.expected_answer: Employer contributions (matching and automatic pay credits) are 100% immediately vested - there is no waiting period, and employees keep the full employer contribution even if they leave the company right away.

cases.query: Until what age are my children covered as dependents on my JPMorgan Chase medical plan?
cases.expected_answer: Children are eligible as dependents until the end of the calendar year in which they turn 26, with no student-status, marital-status, or tax-dependency requirement. Disabled dependent children may remain eligible beyond 26 with documentation and approval.

cases.query: Which medical plan carriers does JPMorgan Chase offer, and is there a low-cost regional option?
cases.expected_answer: The national plans are Aetna, Cigna Healthcare, and UnitedHealthcare. Centivo is a lower-cost regional plan available in select markets (New York metro area, select Texas locations) with a focused provider network.

cases.query: How long do I have to enroll a newborn baby in my health plan after birth?
cases.expected_answer: Newborns must be enrolled within 30 days of birth to ensure continuous coverage; if enrolled on time, coverage is retroactive to the date of birth.

cases.query: How much tuition assistance does JPMorgan Chase provide for a master's degree program in the Guild catalog?
cases.expected_answer: Up to $7,500 per year for master's degree programs in the Guild catalog from accredited institutions, including MBA programs.

cases.query: Do I have to pay back my Guild Education tuition benefit if I quit JPMorgan Chase after finishing my degree?
cases.expected_answer: No. Unlike traditional tuition reimbursement programs, the Guild Education benefit does not require a service commitment or repayment if the employee leaves the company - there is no obligation to stay employed for any period after completing the program. (The one exception is tuition REIMBURSEMENT for programs outside the Guild catalog, where JPMorgan Chase may require repayment if the employee voluntarily terminates within 12 months of reimbursement.)

cases.query: How much of my employer-provided tuition assistance is tax-free per year?
cases.expected_answer: Under IRS Section 127, the first $5,250 of employer-provided educational assistance per calendar year is tax-free. Any amount above $5,250 is taxable income, included in Box 1 wages on the W-2.

cases.query: How many weeks of paid parental leave does JPMorgan Chase provide, and does it differ by gender?
cases.expected_answer: 16 continuous workweeks of fully paid parental leave for all eligible parents, applied on a gender-neutral basis with no distinction between 'primary' and 'secondary' caregiver - available for birth, adoption, or surrogacy placement.

cases.query: How many paid sick days do full-time employees get each year, and does unused sick time carry over?
cases.expected_answer: Full-time employees receive up to 10 sick days (80 hours) per year, granted January 1. Unused sick time does not carry over to the following year and is not paid out upon termination (state/local law exceptions like California and NYC may require carryover).

cases.query: How many days of paid bereavement leave do I get for the death of my spouse versus the death of a sibling?
cases.expected_answer: Up to 20 continuous workdays for the death of a spouse/domestic partner, child, or a miscarriage/stillbirth. Five consecutive workdays for extended family members such as a sibling, parent, or grandparent.

cases.query: How many weeks of unpaid leave am I entitled to under FMLA, and what are the eligibility requirements?
cases.expected_answer: Up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period (26 weeks for military caregiver leave). To be eligible, an employee must have worked at JPMorgan Chase for at least 12 months, worked at least 1,250 hours in the preceding 12 months, and work at a location with 50+ employees within 75 miles.

cases.query: What is Personal Leave and how long can it last, and how much of it is job-protected?
cases.expected_answer: Personal Leave is unpaid leave of up to 26 weeks in a 12-month period for reasons not covered by other policies (e.g. FMLA, STD). Only the first 4 weeks are job-protected; approval beyond that is discretionary and based on business needs.

cases.query: Can I take FMLA leave in small increments, like a few hours at a time for physical therapy appointments?
cases.expected_answer: Yes, this is called intermittent leave - available when medically necessary for a serious health condition (examples given include chemotherapy appointments and physical therapy sessions). It requires medical certification of medical necessity, and is NOT available for birth/adoption bonding, which must be taken continuously.

cases.query: How long is the waiting period before Short-Term Disability benefits start, and can I use sick time during it?
cases.expected_answer: There is a 14-calendar-day elimination (waiting) period before STD benefits begin. Employees may use accrued sick time (or vacation/personal days) during this period; if sick time is exhausted, the employee is on unpaid leave for the remainder of the waiting period.

cases.query: How much of my salary does Short-Term Disability pay if I've worked at JPMorgan Chase for 3 years?
cases.expected_answer: For an employee with 2 but less than 5 years of service, STD pays 10 weeks at 100% of base salary followed by up to 16 weeks at 60% of base salary, for a maximum of 26 weeks total.

cases.query: What percentage of my income does Long-Term Disability replace, and is it reduced if I also get Social Security Disability?
cases.expected_answer: Group LTD replaces 50-60% of Total Annual Cash Compensation depending on election/TACC. Yes - LTD is offset dollar-for-dollar by any approved SSDI benefit, and the employee is required to apply for SSDI once the LTD claim is approved.

cases.query: If I need extended time off for my own serious illness, should I use Personal Leave, FMLA, or Short-Term Disability?
cases.expected_answer: Short-Term Disability is the right fit for an employee's own illness/injury (up to 26 weeks, full or partial pay). FMLA (12 weeks, unpaid but job-protected) typically runs concurrently with STD, providing the job protection while STD provides the pay. Personal Leave is meant for situations NOT covered by FMLA, STD, or other policies - it should be considered only after ruling those out.
cases.notes: Tests whether retrieval pulls from both unpaid_leave.pdf and disability.pdf and synthesizes correctly, since the two documents cross-reference each other's policies.

cases.query: What is the weather like in New York today?
cases.notes: Not answerable from the knowledge base at all. A grounded system should decline or say it doesn't have this information - NOT fabricate a weather report. Fail condition: any confident-sounding answer with a temperature or forecast.

cases.query: What is JPMorgan Chase's stock price target for next quarter?
cases.notes: Plausible-sounding but entirely outside the HR benefits knowledge base (financial/investor content, not a benefits policy). Should decline, not hallucinate a number - this is the classic case that separates a grounded RAG system from a bare LLM.

cases.query: What is the exact dollar amount of the wellness screening financial incentive for 2026?
cases.notes: The real document explicitly says the wellness incentive amount is 'determined annually' without stating a dollar figure - this is a real gap in the source document itself, not a retrieval failure. A grounded answer should say the specific amount isn't stated in this policy rather than inventing a number. Good test of whether the system distinguishes 'not in my sources' from 'not in this specific chunk.'

cases.query: Confirm that JPMorgan Chase provides 20 weeks of paid parental leave.
cases.expected_answer: This premise is incorrect - the real figure is 16 weeks, not 20. A grounded system should correct the false premise rather than agreeing with it.
cases.notes: A leading/false-premise question. Tests whether the model echoes the user's incorrect number (a common failure mode) instead of grounding strictly in retrieved text. The real answer is 16, and the 20-day figure in the KB belongs to a DIFFERENT benefit (bereavement leave for immediate family), which is a plausible source of confusion worth specifically testing.

cases.query: What is the JPMorgan Chase 401(k) match percentage, and how much tuition assistance is available per year for a master's degree in the Guild catalog?
cases.expected_answer: JPMorgan Chase matches 100% of employee contributions (dollar-for-dollar) up to 5% of Eligible Compensation. Separately, tuition assistance covers up to $7,500 per year for master's degree programs in the Guild catalog.
cases.notes: Phase 67 (multi-agentic-rag) - one question spanning two different KB documents/topics (401k.pdf + tuition.pdf, both already covered individually by 401k-01/tuition-01). expected_source_document names only the first topic (401k.pdf) because score_case()'s retrieval metrics compare against a single id, not a list - this case's real purpose is testing whether the Planner splits a same-domain compound question into two focused vector_kb_agent tasks (or covers both well in one), which is checked directly by tests/hrb_chatbot/ai/agents/workflow_agents/test_multi_agent_pipeline_golden_cases.py, not by this file's own exact-match scoring.

cases.query: What is the JPMorgan Chase parental leave policy, and what is my current leave balance?
cases.expected_answer: JPMorgan Chase provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to all eligible employees for the birth, adoption, or surrogacy placement of a child.
cases.notes: Phase 67 (multi-agentic-rag) - one KB question (gradeable) + one live-data question (the caller's own leave balance, via lms_ops_agent/MCP - not stable/known ahead of time, so not reduced to a fixed expected value). expected_answer/expected_keywords cover only the KB half; this case is scored by this file's harness for that half only. The live-balance half is checked for routing/coherence (did the Planner dispatch both agents, did the Reviewer produce one answer covering both) by tests/hrb_chatbot/ai/agents/workflow_agents/test_multi_agent_pipeline_golden_cases.py, not by exact-match scoring here. Phase 73 finding, fixed by Phase 151: this query's text also matches genai-rag's own try_route_to_mcp() keyword bypass ('leave balance') - run through genai-rag's pipeline.answer_query() directly (not multi-agentic-rag), the whole compound question used to be hijacked to the MCP-only answer, losing the parental-leave-policy half entirely. call_type changed from 'agent_call' to 'mixed_call' here because that's what this case actually is - neither a pure MCP bypass nor a pure LLM call - the 'agent_call' label was encoding the bug (full MCP bypass) as the expected outcome, not describing genuinely correct behavior. Phase 151 removed genai-rag's top-level keyword shortcut entirely, so this case no longer bypasses the LLM - excluded from both test_agent_call_cases_bypass_the_llm_entirely (would wrongly expect full bypass) and test_llm_call_cases_do_not_accidentally_match_mcp_keywords (this query genuinely does match MCP keywords, just no longer exclusively) by using a call_type neither test's loop filters for.

cases.query: What is my current leave balance?
cases.notes: Phase 73 - dedicated case for the routing-type check (test_routing_type_golden_cases.py), not for answer-quality scoring. Exercises genai-rag's try_route_to_mcp() deterministic bypass (Phase 49) - a real MCP call, not retrieval+generation, so no fixed expected_answer/expected_source_document is meaningful here.

cases.query: What unpaid leave requests have I submitted in the past?
cases.notes: Phase 258 - routing-accuracy case, not answer-quality scoring (same reasoning as agent-call-leave-balance-01). Real leave-history data, not a KB document lookup.

cases.query: How many employees took parental leave last year?
cases.notes: Phase 258 - best-effort routing case, flagged honestly: lms_analytics_agent's real planner-routing trigger wasn't live-verified before adding this (the Planner's own routing decision is itself an LLM judgment call, not deterministic) - confirm with a real run before trusting this case's expected_agent value. No single-agentic-rag equivalent tool exists for this kind of aggregate question, so expected_tool is intentionally omitted. call_type is llm_call, not agent_call - this query does NOT match genai-rag's own deterministic MCP-bypass keywords (confirmed live via test_routing_type_golden_cases.py, which caught this exact mistake on the first attempt), unlike agent-call-leave-balance-01/routing-leave-history-01 above - it's only an 'agent_call' in the multi-agentic-rag planner-routing sense, a different mechanism.
